user.title: Add an Aerohive, Extreme Networks or OpenWrt device
user.description: Find access points, routers and switches on your network automatically, or enter an IP address yourself. OpenWrt devices are added by IP address with their SSH login.

manual.title: Enter device details
manual.description: Connect to an access point or branch router over SSH. Provide a password, an SSH private key path, or both.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the device.
data_description.ssh_key_path: Absolute path to a private key file readable by Home Assistant, e.g. /config/.ssh/aerohive.
data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between polls. Keep this at 60 or higher for a BR100.

pick.title: Pick a discovered device
pick.description: Found {count} likely Aerohive/Extreme device(s) out of {total} SSH devices. Each shows its IP address, name, model, MAC address and where it's connected, when known. Pick one (or type an IP) and enter its CLI login.

data_description.ssh_key_path: Absolute path to a private key file readable by Home Assistant, e.g. /config/.ssh/aerohive.
data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between polls. Keep this at 60 or higher for a BR100.

discovery_confirm.title: Set up {name}

data_description.ssh_key_path: Absolute path to a private key file readable by Home Assistant, e.g. /config/.ssh/aerohive.
data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between polls. Keep this at 60 or higher for a BR100.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate
reauth_confirm.description: The device rejected the stored credentials.

opnsense.title: OPNsense router
opnsense.description: Connects with OPNsense's REST API, not SSH. In OPNsense, create an API key under System → Access → Users (edit a user → API keys → +); you get a file with the key and secret. A user with read access to the dashboard, diagnostics, interfaces and gateways is enough to monitor the router; rebooting needs System: Firmware or full access.

data_description.verify_ssl: Leave off for OPNsense's own self-signed certificate. Turn on if the router has a trusted certificate.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect. Check host, port and that SSH is enabled on the device.
error.invalid_key: The SSH key file could not be read.
error.password_or_key: Enter a password or an SSH key path.
error.no_devices_found: No devices found by the network scan. Enter the IP address manually.

abort.already_in_progress: Setup for this device is already in progress.
abort.not_aerohive_device: This device isn't an Aerohive / Extreme Networks access point or switch.

progress.scanning: Scanning the local network for SSH devices. This takes up to about 15 seconds.

data.raw_sensors: Create sensors for every raw field

data_description.tracked_clients: Create a device tracker and detail sensors (signal, SNR, rates, SSID) only for these client MAC addresses (pick from connected clients or type a MAC).
data_description.detailed_stats: Throughput and counters for Ethernet ports and SSID sub-interfaces, plus CPU and memory. Adds a few CLI commands per poll; turn off for a slow BR100.
data_description.raw_sensors: One sensor (disabled by default) for every other field the CLI reports, so you can enable anything you need.
data_description.enable_all_entities: Turn on every entity, including the diagnostic ones that are disabled by default (counters, raw fields, port switches).

wifi.title: Wi-Fi networks
wifi.description:
{message}

Pick a network to change its password, where it broadcasts, or to delete it. Or add a new one.

wifi_edit.title: Edit {ssid}
wifi_edit.description:
{message}

Leave the password empty to keep the current one. Changes are applied together and saved on the device.

data_description.password: 8-63 characters. The current password can't be shown: the device stores it encrypted.
data_description.radios: Untick every radio to stop broadcasting without deleting the network.

data_description.password: WPA2-PSK, 8-63 characters. Leave empty for an open network.
data_description.access_points: Create it on these access points.

wifi_delete.title: Delete {ssid}?
wifi_delete.description: This removes the network from the device and saves the configuration. Clients connected to it will be disconnected.

error.invalid_mac: One of the entries is not a valid MAC address.
error.invalid_password: The password must be 8-63 printable characters, without double quotes.
error.invalid_ssid_name: The name must be 1-32 printable characters, without double quotes.
error.ssid_exists: A network with this name already exists.

abort.device_unavailable: The device isn't reachable right now. Try again in a minute.

run_show_command.name: Run show command
run_show_command.description: Run a read-only 'show' command on the device and return the raw output (for capturing parser samples).

command.name: Command
command.description: A command starting with 'show', e.g. 'show station'.

redact.name: Redact secrets
redact.description: Mask key/password arguments in the output.

set_ssid_password.name: Set SSID password
set_ssid_password.description: Change the WPA2-PSK key of an SSID and save the configuration.

password.name: Password
password.description: New key, 8-63 printable ASCII characters (no double quotes).

security_object.name: Security object
security_object.description: Security-object name. Looked up in the running config if omitted (falls back to the SSID name).

disconnect_client.name: Disconnect client
disconnect_client.description: De-authenticate a wireless client by MAC address.

mac.name: MAC address
mac.description: Client MAC address in any common format.

create_ssid.name: Create SSID
create_ssid.description: Create a new Wi-Fi network (security-object + SSID) and broadcast it, then save the configuration.

password.name: Password
password.description: WPA2-PSK key (8-63 characters). Leave empty for an open network.

radios.name: Radios
radios.description: Radios to broadcast on, e.g. wifi0, wifi1. Default: all active radios.

delete_ssid.name: Delete SSID
delete_ssid.description: Stop broadcasting an SSID and remove it (and its own security-object) from the configuration.

power_cycle_poe.name: Power cycle PoE port
power_cycle_poe.description: Turn PoE off for 5 seconds and on again (switches).

set_port.name: Enable or disable a port
set_port.description: Turn an Ethernet port on or off and save the configuration. Uplink ports are protected unless force is set.

force.name: Force
force.description: Also allow turning off an uplink port (may disconnect Home Assistant from the device).

backup_config.name: Back up configuration
backup_config.description: Read the device's configuration and save it to a backup file in Home Assistant (skipped if nothing changed since the last backup).

list_backups.name: List configuration backups
list_backups.description: List the configuration backups stored for a device.

save_config.name: Save configuration
save_config.description: Save the running configuration on the device so it survives a reboot or power loss.

restore_config.name: Restore configuration
restore_config.description: Send a configuration backup back to the device line by line. Lines the device rejects are reported; nothing is saved on the device unless save is on.

file.name: Backup file
file.description: File name from List configuration backups. Default: the latest backup.

save.name: Save on the device
save.description: Save the configuration on the device after restoring.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Must be on: restoring changes the device configuration.

set_poe.name: Turn PoE on or off
set_poe.description: Turn Power over Ethernet on or off for one switch port and save the configuration.

set_port_description.name: Name a port
set_port_description.description: Set a switch port's display name (ExtremeXOS display string, up to 15 characters without spaces). Leave the name empty to clear it.

description.name: Name
description.description: New name, e.g. camera-1. Empty clears it.

reboot.name: Reboot
reboot.description: Reboot the device. On ExtremeXOS with unsaved changes the reboot is refused unless save changes is set, so nothing is lost by accident.

save_changes.name: Save changes
save_changes.description: On: save unsaved configuration changes first. Off: reboot and lose them. Not set: refuse if there are unsaved changes.

accept_config.name: Accept current configuration
accept_config.description: Use the device's current configuration as the new known-good backup and clear the 'configuration changed after reboot' alert.

refresh.name: Refresh now
refresh.description: Read everything from a device right away, including LLDP neighbours, health and the configuration. Without a device, every device is refreshed.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The device to refresh. Leave empty for all devices.

set_ssid.name: Change a Wi-Fi network
set_ssid.description: Turn a Wi-Fi network on or off (optionally for a while), choose its bands, hide it or limit its clients, on every access point that has it or on one.

device_id.name: Access point
device_id.description: Only this access point. Leave empty for every access point with the network.

enabled.name: On
enabled.description: Broadcast the network (on the chosen bands, or all) or stop broadcasting it.

max_clients.name: Max clients
max_clients.description: Most devices allowed on the network per access point.

duration.name: For
duration.description: Only for this long; afterwards the network goes back to how it was (also after a restart). Needs On.

approve_device.name: Approve a device
approve_device.description: Approve a device waiting on the onboarding portal: it gets its own Wi-Fi key and the portal shows it the password. For automations, e.g. a button on a phone notification. Administrators only.

request_id.name: Request
request_id.description: The id from the aerohive_local_onboarding_request event.

wifi.name: Wi-Fi network
wifi.description: ID of a Wi-Fi network with per-device keys. Default: the device kind's rule, what the device asked for, or the first offered network.

network.name: Network
network.description: ID of the network (VLAN) the device lands in. Default: the rule's, else the Wi-Fi's own network.

minutes.name: Valid for
minutes.description: Minutes until the key stops working. Empty: permanent (or the rule's duration).

bind_mac.name: Only for this device's MAC address
bind_mac.description: Tie the key to the MAC address the device used on the onboarding Wi-Fi. Leave off for phones and laptops (they use private addresses).

decline_device.name: Decline a device
decline_device.description: Decline a device waiting on the onboarding portal; the portal tells it so. Administrators only.

request_id.name: Request
request_id.description: The id from the aerohive_local_onboarding_request event.

set_port_speed.name: Set port speed
set_port_speed.description: Set a switch or router port's speed and duplex, or back to auto-negotiation. ExtremeXOS: documented commands; SR switches and HiveOS Ethernet ports: assumed commands (not yet confirmed on a device).

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The switch, router or access point.

port.name: Port
port.description: The port as shown in the Network panel, e.g. 5 (ExtremeXOS), 1/0/3 (SR switch) or eth1.

speed.name: Speed
speed.description: auto, or 10, 100, 1000 or 10000 Mbit/s (what the port supports).

duplex.name: Duplex
duplex.description: full or half for 10/100 Mbit/s. Default: full (auto with Auto speed).

force.name: Force
force.description: Also change an uplink port, which can disconnect Home Assistant from the device.

config_changed_after_reboot.title: {device}: configuration changed after a reboot
config_changed_after_reboot.description:
After its last reboot, {device} is running a configuration that differs from the backup taken on {backup} ({added} line(s) added, {removed} removed). This is what happens when unsaved changes are lost in a power cut, or the device boots an old or default configuration.

Changes:
```
{changes}
```

- If the backup is correct, run the **Restore configuration** action (`aerohive_local.restore_config`) for this device, with `save: true`.
- If the current configuration is correct, press **Accept current configuration** on the device page.

No new backup is taken until you do one of these, so the last known-good one stays available.

boot_config_problem.title: {device}: did not boot as configured
boot_config_problem.description:
{device} reports: {problems}.

This usually follows a power loss or a corrupted configuration file. Check `show switch` on the device. To boot the saved configuration again, run `use configuration primary` and then `reboot` on the switch, or restore the latest backup with the **Restore configuration** action.
